business.title: What kind of business is this?
business.description: e.g. 'a small publisher', 'a café in Portland'.

tools.name: desk_status
tools.description: The support desk now: every ticket that needs a reply (urgent first, then oldest) with what the customer asked and whether a reply is drafted, what waits on the customer, the questions no help article answers yet, and the help articles in kb/. Every ticket has its id. Call it first when asked about the queue.

tools.name: add_ticket
tools.description: Log a customer request as a ticket: subject, customer, channel, category, priority, their message in their words, and the day it came in (YYYY-MM-DD, default today). The same subject from the same customer updates the open ticket, never duplicates it. Call it as soon as a request is mentioned, before you describe it.

tools.name: suggest_reply
tools.description: Save a suggested reply on a ticket, ready for the person to send, with the help article in kb/ it draws on. When no article answers the question, pass gap with a short topic (reuse a topic from the status) so it shows as a knowledge-base gap. Call it as soon as the reply is drafted, before you show it.

tools.name: set_ticket_status
tools.description: Move a ticket: open (being worked on), waiting (on the customer), resolved, or back to new. Call it the moment the person says a ticket moved.

tools.name: save_kb_article
tools.description: Write a help article to kb/ (title and markdown body) and close the knowledge-base gap it answers (topic, as the status names it). Saving the same title again updates the article. Leave prices, dates and policies the business has not stated as [bracketed] blanks. Call it as soon as the article is written, before you describe it.

tools.name: list_tickets
tools.description: Every ticket, resolved ones too, with its status, category, customer, age and message.

tools.name: page_suggest_reply
tools.description: Save a reply on a ticket.
